newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen up by 3,000-15,000T - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen up by 3,000-15,000T - trade.

text.p: Metal traders in Singapore expected a build in copper stocks on the London Metal Exchange (LME) later on Tuesday but estimates for the rise were far apart, ranging between 3,000 tonnes and 15,000 tonnes.
"Copper stocks could rise by around 15,000 tonnes," said a trader with a European firm.
"The fall of three-month copper prices on Monday, down from a high of $2,200 to $2,173 is evident that stocks will rise," said a broker.
"We do not expect such a large jump this time unlike the hike in stocks seen last week," said a Japanese trader.
LME copper stocks surged by 26,100 tonnes on Friday to 191,750 tonnes.
Aluminium stocks were also expected to increase by between 1,500-2,000 tonnes, while zinc inventories are seen falling by around 1,000 to 2,000 tonnes.

A chartist said the copper market is firm but he expected three-month prices to ease gradually by $20-$30 a tonne from indications around $2,173/$2,178 at 0600 GMT in Asian trade. Copper was quoted at $2,173 at London's close on Monday.

He said prices could "take a break" during the Chinese and Moslem festive season this week to settle around $2,140-$2,150, but added that he was uncertain where the market would head after the holidays.
"When the backwardation disappears, it is a signal that the market will ease," said the broker.
The copper backwardation, or cash to three-month premium, is expected to narrow in the near term from the current $180 to $150, traders said.
Traders also projected stocks in Singapore would rise marginally on Tuesday. "Some copper stocks will be heading towards Singapore," said one trader.
LME warehouse stocks in Singapore fell to 45,000 tonnes on Friday down from 40,575 tonnes in the previous report.
Three-month aluminium prices were expected to stay within a range of $1,650-$1,680 a tonne, with one trader pegging near term support at $1,550.
